subject: Next steps: dedicated GPU pool sizing, isolation & procurement path
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Charles Harris <charles.harris@helixcure.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Next steps: dedicated GPU pool sizing, isolation & procurement path

Hi Charles — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum:  

Call summary (what we heard)
- Primary pain: model inference variability during peak training infer bursts (latency spikes) and security requirement to isolate sensitive models from other tenants.
- Business goal: migrate critical inference for real-time triage to a dedicated pool with predictable latency SLAs and strict network isolation by Q4 2027.
- Target traffic: steady-state 8–12 concurrent streams with peak bursts up to ~35 concurrent requests; throughput expectation ~500k tokens/day initially.

Redwood proposal (high level)
- Dedicated reserved pool: 10x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) with private tenancy and VPC peering.
- Isolation: single-tenant pool + encrypted KV cache; optional on-prem proxy if you need air-gapped access.
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime (monthly) and P95 latency target of 120ms for 512-token requests.

Immediate next steps (proposed timeline)
1) We’ll share a draft SLA & pricing worksheet by EOD tomorrow. [Attachment: redwood_sla_draft.pdf; pricing-quote-helix-10gpus.xlsx]
2) HelixCure to confirm: procurement contact, PO timing, and any mandatory vendor paperwork (SOC2, DPA).
3) Technical kickoff / POC planning: Rishi to run a sizing exercise and confirm autoscaling policy (target: 2-week POC).
4) Security questionnaire: if you have a standard vendor form, send it to security@redwood.com; we’ll prioritize responses.

Open questions from our side
- Do you require hard multi-tenant isolation (no shared kernel/host) or is network/NIC-level isolation sufficient?
- Expected contract start date (we suggested 2027-08-01 as target).

Thanks — I’ll be on standby to move the paperwork.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
[Attachment: redwood_sla_draft.pdf (PDF, 48KB), pricing-quote-helix-10gpus.xlsx (XLSX, 72KB)]

From: Charles Harris <charles.harris@helixcure.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Kovacs <elena.kovacs@helixcure.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 20:27:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Next steps: dedicated GPU pool sizing, isolation & procurement path

Thanks Stephanie — useful recap, appreciate the clarity. A couple of clarifications from our side:  

Confirmation & asks
- We are aligned on the need for a single-tenant pool. For compliance reasons we need to avoid shared host kernels where possible; network/NIC isolation alone is not sufficient.
- Procurement contact: Elena Kovacs (cc'd) will own the PO and vendor onboarding. Elena, our target is to have contracts signed and PO issued by 2027-07-15; is that feasible?
- SOC2: we need your SOC2 Type II report and the DPA (data processing addendum) as part of vendor review. Please send to vendorops@helixcure.ai.

PO/terms note
- We typically do a 12-month reserved commitment with quarterly invoicing and a 30-day termination clause for change-of-control events. Pricing will be reviewed by our finance team but good to get your initial worksheet.

Next steps for us
- Elena will route the vendor packet internally and share the vendor intake form.
- We’re happy to schedule a 30–45 minute technical deep-dive with your infra lead next week. Suggest Wed 2027-05-18 14:00 PT if that works for Rishi.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Charles
Charles Harris
Head of Infrastructure | HelixCure
charles.harris@helixcure.ai | +1 212-555-0137
[External: vendorops@helixcure.ai, Elena Kovacs <elena.kovacs@helixcure.ai>]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Next steps: dedicated GPU pool sizing, isolation & procurement path

Looping back with a quick technical note after reviewing the call notes and Charles' reply. TL;DR — feasible within proposed window, minor ops items to confirm.

Technical feasibility & recommendations
- Isolation: we can provision a single-tenant pool using dedicated hosts (no shared kernel) and separate NVMe volumes per customer. That meets HelixCure's compliance ask. We’ll include HSM/KMS integration for key material.
- Pool sizing: 10x A100-equivalent should cover steady-state + expected bursts with headroom. For safety during POC, recommend a 12-GPU temporary burst window (short-term burst capacity) to avoid saturation during initial testing.
- Autoscaling & caching: prefer conservative batching for latency-sensitive flows; enable prefix KV caching for common prompts which will reduce token cost by ~18% in our benchmarks.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime we can commit to in a reserved model; P95 latency target of ~120ms depends on exact sequence length and pipeline (we’ll validate with your sample traces).

Attachments & ops items (for procurement)
- I’ve uploaded: isolation_arch.png (arch diagram), redwood_sla_draft.pdf (SLA + terms), pricing-quote-helix-10gpus.xlsx (formal quote). Please attach these to the vendor packet.
- Action: Stephanie to share SOC2 link + DPA to vendorops@helixcure.ai; I’ll join the intake call Wed 2027-05-18 14:00 PT.

Questions for procurement/ops
- Is HelixCure ok with quarterly invoicing on a 12-month reserved term (standard)? Any internal approvals that typically add time?
- Do they need us to sign a redlined MSA or will they accept our standard terms with a simple DPA?

I’ll prepare a short POC checklist by EOD today that includes test prompts, expected load profile, and success criteria.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0124
